title: 512-Point FFT Time on RP2350 @ 150 MHz: Our Result vs. Published Libraries
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing / Embedded Systems
description: Horizontal bar chart comparing 512-point FFT execution time on the RP2350 @ 150 MHz across our best assembly kernel and two published implementations

educational.topic: 512-Point FFT Time on RP2350 @ 150 MHz: Our Result vs. Published Libraries
learningObjectives: Compare FFT execution time across implementations only when the board and clock speed are held constant
Explain why scaling a benchmark from a different transform size (N log2 N) produces an estimate, not a measurement
Interpret the performance gap between hand-tuned assembly, bare-metal C++, and interpreted MicroPython on the same core
prerequisites: FFT computational complexity O(N log N)

keyQuestions: Why is it only fair to compare these three implementations because they share a board and clock speed?
What does it mean that two of the three bars are 'scaled' rather than directly measured?
commonMisconceptions: Assuming any two published FFT benchmarks are comparable regardless of board, clock speed, or transform size
